title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
signature: int Solve(int[] heights, int bricks, int ladders)
statement: You start on building 0 and move to the next building each step. Going down or staying level is free. Going UP by d costs either d bricks or one ladder, and a ladder covers any height. Return the index of the furthest building you can reach.
constraints: descents and level moves are always free
return an INDEX, not a count of buildings
hints: Ladders are the scarce resource and they are worth most on the biggest climbs - but you do not know which climbs are biggest until you have seen them.
So commit ladders greedily to every climb as you meet it, and take one back later when a bigger climb turns up.

Keep the ladder-assigned climbs in a MIN-heap. When a new climb arrives and no ladders remain, pop the smallest ladder climb; if the new climb is bigger, give it the ladder and pay bricks for the small one instead. Run out of bricks and the previous index is the answer.

cases.name: descents are free but the climb still stops you
ladder saved for the big climb
